question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pulakesin II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harshavardhana's ambition of extending his empire into the Deccan and South India was checked by the Chalukya ruler Pulakesin II, who defeated him on the banks of the river Narmada (around 618–619 CE). (हर्षवर्धन को पुलकेशिन द्वितीय ने रोका)

• After this defeat, the Narmada became the southern boundary of Harsha's empire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti/Vardhana dynasty ruled from Thanesar and later Kannauj. The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited his court, and the court poet Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita.

• Pulakesin II (610–642 CE) belonged to the Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi). His victory over Harsha is recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by his court poet Ravikirti.

• Pulakesin II was later defeated and killed by the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I of Kanchi.

NOTE

• Rajaraja I was the great Chola ruler (985–1014 CE) who built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur. Ashoka was the Mauryan emperor (3rd century BCE) — both belong to entirely different periods.

question: When was India’s first ever budget presented?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1860.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first ever budget was presented on 7 April 1860 by James Wilson, the first Finance Member of the India Council under the British Crown. (भारत का पहला बजट — 1860)

• It was introduced after the Revolt of 1857, to repair the finances of the government; Wilson also introduced income tax in India in the same budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• James Wilson was also the founder of *The Economist* magazine and of the Chartered Bank (later Standard Chartered).

• The first budget of independent India was presented on 26 November 1947 by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty.

• The first budget of the Republic of India was presented by John Mathai in 1950.

NOTE

• Morarji Desai presented the maximum number of budgets (10). Indira Gandhi was the first woman to present a budget (1970), and Nirmala Sitharaman is the first full-time woman Finance Minister to do so (from 2019). The budget timing was shifted from 5 p.m. to 11 a.m. in 2001, and the Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

question: The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is zone of exclusion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clear region of cytoplasm surrounding the Golgi complex (Golgi apparatus), which is free of ribosomes and other cell organelles, is called the "zone of exclusion" (also known as the Golgi ground substance). (गोल्जी काय के चारों ओर का स्वच्छ क्षेत्र — ज़ोन ऑफ़ एक्सक्लूज़न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Camillo Golgi (1898). It consists of flattened sacs (cisternae), tubules and vesicles.

• Functions of the Golgi body: packaging, processing and dispatch of proteins and lipids, formation of lysosomes, and synthesis of cell wall material in plants. It is called the "post office of the cell" or the "traffic police of the cell".

NOTE

• Cytosol is the fluid part of the cytoplasm; cytosine is a nitrogenous base of DNA/RNA (a pyrimidine); cytochrome is a haem-containing protein of the electron transport chain in mitochondria. None of these describes a region around the Golgi body.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture?

i. Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial.

ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddh

iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and ii.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, statements i and ii are correct while statement iii is incorrect.

◦ Statement i is correct — an "Uddeshika (Uddesika) stupa" is a commemorative/memorial stupa, built to mark an event or to commemorate the Buddha and his disciples. (स्मारक स्तूप)

◦ Statement ii is accepted as correct in the key — the "Paribhogika stupa" is the second recognised category of stupa in this classification.

◦ Statement iii is incorrect — the Bharhut stupa is situated in Madhya Pradesh (Satna district), not in Uttar Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Traditional classification of stupas: Saririka (containing the bodily relics of the Buddha or saints), Paribhogika (containing objects used by the Buddha, such as his bowl or robe) and Uddeshika (commemorative, built at sacred spots).

• The Bharhut Stupa (2nd century BCE, Shunga period) is famous for its carved railings and torana, now preserved largely in the Indian Museum, Kolkata. It was discovered by Alexander Cunningham in 1873.

• The Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh), originally built by Ashoka, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Key elements of a stupa: Anda (hemispherical dome), Harmika (railing on top), Yashti (central mast), Chhatra (umbrella), Medhi (drum/base) and Pradakshina Patha (circumambulatory path).

question: If an Indian citizen is denied entry to a public place because of his caste, which of the following Fundamental Rights is denied to him?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to equality.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Denying a citizen entry to a public place on the ground of caste violates the "Right to Equality" guaranteed under Articles 14–18 of the Constitution. (समानता का अधिकार)

• Specifically, Article 15(2) states that no citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, be subjected to any disability regarding access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

• Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

• Article 16 — equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

• Article 17 — abolition of untouchability.

• Article 18 — abolition of titles.

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12–35): Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30) and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). The Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

question: ‘Ram Navami’ is celebrated in India to commemorate the:
option_2: coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
option_3: return of Lord Rama from forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is birth of Lord Rama.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ram Navami" is celebrated to commemorate the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh incarnation (avatar) of Lord Vishnu. (राम नवमी — भगवान राम का जन्मोत्सव)

• It falls on the ninth day (Navami) of the Shukla Paksha in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April) and marks the last day of Chaitra Navratri.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord Rama was born at Ayodhya to King Dasharatha and Queen Kausalya. The Ramayana, composed by Maharishi Valmiki, narrates his life; Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.

• Ram Navami is celebrated with great fervour at Ayodhya (UP), Sitamarhi (Bihar), Rameswaram (Tamil Nadu) and Bhadrachalam (Telangana).

NOTE

• Related festivals: Dussehra/Vijayadashami marks the killing of Ravana; Deepavali marks the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile; Janmashtami marks the birth of Lord Krishna.

question: In February 2024, who took an oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champai Soren.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2024, Champai Soren took the oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand, after Hemant Soren resigned following his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate. (चंपई सोरेन — झारखंड के 12वें मुख्यमंत्री)

• He belonged to the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) at that time and is popularly called the "Tiger of Kolhan" for his role in the statehood movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda) and is the 28th state of India. Its capital is Ranchi.

• Babulal Marandi was the first Chief Minister of Jharkhand.

• Arjun Munda has also served as Chief Minister of Jharkhand and later as a Union Minister for Tribal Affairs.

NOTE

• A Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164. Jharkhand's Governor at that time was C. P. Radhakrishnan. The state's High Court is at Ranchi, and its major festivals include Sarhul, Karma and Sohrai.

question: Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 for which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Art - Playback Singing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The renowned singer Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 in the field of "Art – Playback Singing". (उदित नारायण — पद्म भूषण 2016, पार्श्व गायन)

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri in 2009.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Udit Narayan is a multiple National Film Award winner, famous for songs in films such as *Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak*, *Lagaan* and *Dil To Pagal Hai*. He was born in Nepal and raised in Bihar.

• The Padma Awards, instituted in 1954, are announced every year on Republic Day (26 January) and conferred by the President of India.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna (highest) > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. Padma Bhushan is given for "distinguished service of a high order" in any field.

question: Which river is known as ‘Langchen Khambab’ in Tibet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sutlej.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sutlej river is known as "Langchen Khambab" in Tibet, which means "flowing from the mouth of the elephant". (सतलुज — लांगचेन खंबाब)

• It rises from the Rakas Tal (Rakshastal) lake near Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass in Himachal Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab and is an antecedent river (older than the Himalayas). The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on it.

• Tibetan names of Himalayan rivers: Indus – Singi Khamban ("from the lion's mouth"); Brahmaputra – Tsangpo ("the purifier"); Karnali/Ghaghara – Tamchok Khambab.

• The five rivers of Punjab: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

NOTE

• As per the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India has full rights over the Eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan gets the Western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

question: Bal Gangadhar described ______ as a diamond of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak described Gopal Krishna Gokhale as "the Diamond of India, the Jewel of Maharashtra and the Prince of Workers". (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — भारत का हीरा)

• The tribute is famous because Tilak (an Extremist) and Gokhale (a Moderate) held opposing political views, yet Tilak praised him warmly on his death in 1915.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866–1915) was a leading Moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, its President in 1905 (Banaras session), and the founder of the Servants of India Society (1905).

• He was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhi called him his political mentor; Gokhale in turn advised Gandhi to travel across India before entering politics.

NOTE

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was called "Lokmanya" and the "Father of Indian Unrest" (by Valentine Chirol). His famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it." He started the Ganpati and Shivaji festivals and published Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English).

question: ‘The Blue Umbrella’, ‘The Cherry Tree’, ‘The Hidden Pool’ are novels written by who among the following authors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Blue Umbrella", "The Cherry Tree" and "The Hidden Pool" were written by the celebrated Indian author Ruskin Bond. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

• His writing is set largely in the hills of Uttarakhand (Mussoorie, Dehradun and Landour) and is loved for its simplicity and its portrayal of nature and childhood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other famous works of Ruskin Bond: *The Room on the Roof* (his first novel, which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957), *A Flight of Pigeons* (the basis of the film *Junoon*), *Rusty* series, *Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra* (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1992).

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

• *The Blue Umbrella* was made into a National Award-winning Hindi film by Vishal Bhardwaj.

NOTE

• Anant Pai ("Uncle Pai") created Amar Chitra Katha and Tinkle; Sudha Murthy wrote *Wise and Otherwise*, *Dollar Bahu* and *How I Taught My Grandmother to Read*; Twinkle Khanna wrote *Mrs Funnybones* and *The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad*.

question: What is the overarching programme introduced in the Union Budget, 2018-19 by Government of India, for the school education sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samagra Shiksha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Samagra Shiksha" is the overarching (integrated) programme for the school education sector announced in the Union Budget 2018-19. It treats school education holistically from pre-school to Class XII. (समग्र शिक्षा)

• It subsumed three earlier schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) and Teacher Education (TE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development). Its main outcome focus is on improving quality, equity and inclusion in school education.

• Samagra Shiksha 2.0 was aligned with the recommendations of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

NOTE

• Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 — implemented from 1 April 2010 under Article 21A (inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002) — provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years. "Rashtriya Unnat Shiksha Abhiyan" and "Sarva Vidya Abhiyan" are not the names of this programme (the higher-education scheme is RUSA — Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan).

question: Who was the highest run scorer in Men’s World Cup cricket - 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohit Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rohit Sharma was the highest run scorer of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2019, scoring 648 runs in the tournament. (रोहित शर्मा — 2019 विश्व कप के सर्वाधिक रन)

• He also became the first batsman to score five centuries in a single World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup was hosted by England and Wales. England won the title for the first time, beating New Zealand in a dramatic final at Lord's decided on boundary count after a tied Super Over.

• Kane Williamson (New Zealand) was the Player of the Tournament; Mitchell Starc (Australia) was the leading wicket-taker with 27 wickets.

NOTE

• India has won the ODI World Cup twice — 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (MS Dhoni) — and the T20 World Cup in 2007 (MS Dhoni) and 2024 (Rohit Sharma). Rohit Sharma holds the record for the highest individual ODI score — 264.

question: The approximate number of water molecules present in 9 gm of water is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.011 × 10²³.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Step 1 — Molar mass of water (H₂O) = (2 × 1) + 16 = 18 g/mol.

• Step 2 — Number of moles = given mass ÷ molar mass = 9 ÷ 18 = 0.5 mole.

• Step 3 — Number of molecules = number of moles × Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³)

◦ = 0.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²³ molecules. (जल के अणुओं की संख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Avogadro's number (N_A) = 6.022 × 10²³ is the number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions) present in one mole of any substance.

• 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 litres at STP (0 °C and 1 atm).

• The concept was named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro; the constant itself was determined later.

NOTE

• Useful formulae: Moles = mass / molar mass = number of particles / 6.022 × 10²³ = volume at STP / 22.4 L. In 9 g of water there are 0.5 mole of H₂O molecules but 1 mole of hydrogen atoms (since each molecule has 2 H atoms).

question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allan Octavian Hume.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant of the Indian Civil Service, was the founder of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885. (ए. ओ. ह्यूम — भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के संस्थापक, 1885)

• The first session of the INC was held in December 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, attended by 72 delegates, and was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A. O. Hume is also called the "Father of the Indian National Congress" and, for his work in ornithology, the "Father of Indian Ornithology".

• The INC was originally planned to be held in Poona, but was shifted to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak.

• Other early leaders: Dadabhai Naoroji (called the Grand Old Man of India, who gave the Drain of Wealth theory), Surendranath Banerjee and Pherozeshah Mehta.

NOTE

• Annie Besant became the first woman President of the INC (Calcutta, 1917) and started the Home Rule Movement (1916); Mahatma Gandhi returned to India in 1915; C. F. Andrews ("Deenabandhu") was a close associate of Gandhi — none of them founded the Congress.

question: Who among the following was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527 CE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rana Sanga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Battle of Khanwa (17 March 1527), Babur defeated Rana Sanga (Rana Sangram Singh) of Mewar. (खानवा का युद्ध, 1527 — राणा सांगा की पराजय)

• This victory destroyed Rajput resistance to Mughal expansion and firmly established Mughal rule in northern India. Babur assumed the title "Ghazi" after this battle.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Babur's key battles: First Battle of Panipat (1526) — defeated Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire; Khanwa (1527) — defeated Rana Sanga; Chanderi (1528) — defeated Medini Rai; Ghaghra (1529) — defeated the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi.

• Babur introduced the Tulughma (flanking) war tactic and the Araba (cart) formation along with gunpowder artillery in India.

NOTE

• Babur wrote his memoirs, the "Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)", in Chagatai Turkish; it was later translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan. Hasan Khan Mewati fought alongside Rana Sanga at Khanwa and was killed there.

question: Where was the inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) organised in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023 was held in Mumbai, at the Dr D. Y. Patil Sports Academy, Navi Mumbai, on 4 March 2023. (डब्ल्यूपीएल 2023 का उद्घाटन मैच — मुंबई)

• The opening match was played between the Mumbai Indians and the Gujarat Giants, and Mumbai Indians won it comfortably.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Mumbai Indians, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, won the first WPL title (2023), defeating the Delhi Capitals in the final.

• The WPL is organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and has five franchises: Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, UP Warriorz and Gujarat Giants.

• Royal Challengers Bangalore won the 2024 edition.

NOTE

• India's women's cricket milestones: Mithali Raj (highest run scorer in women's ODIs), Jhulan Goswami (highest wicket-taker in women's ODIs) and Harmanpreet Kaur (current captain). India were runners-up in the 2017 Women's ODI World Cup and the 2020 Women's T20 World Cup.

question: ‘Chakyar Koothu’, the folk dance form in which the entire story is presented by a single performer, primarily belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chakyar Koothu" is a traditional solo performing art of Kerala, in which a single performer (the Chakyar) narrates the entire story — usually episodes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas — with expressive gestures and witty social commentary. (चाक्यार कूथु — केरल)

• It is performed inside the Koothambalam (the temple theatre) and is accompanied by the Mizhavu drum and cymbals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala's other art forms: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (classical dances), Koodiyattam (the oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Ottamthullal, Theyyam, Kalaripayattu (martial art) and Chavittu Nadakam.

• Ottamthullal, created by Kunchan Nambiar, is called the "poor man's Kathakali" and is also a solo form.

NOTE

• Folk/tribal dances by state: Tripura – Hojagiri; Sikkim – Singhi Chham, Maruni; Tamil Nadu – Karagattam, Kummi, Kolattam, Therukoothu; Kerala – Chakyar Koothu, Theyyam, Thiruvathirakali.

question: Which of the following sectors had the largest percentage of workforce in urban India in the year 2019-2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Service.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In urban India during 2019-2020, the largest share of the workforce was engaged in the "Service (tertiary) sector". (सेवा क्षेत्र — शहरी भारत में सर्वाधिक कार्यबल)

• Urban employment is dominated by trade, transport, communication, banking, insurance, education, health, IT and other services, whereas agriculture dominates rural employment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three sectors of the economy: Primary (agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining), Secondary (manufacturing, construction — industry) and Tertiary (services).

• The services sector contributes the largest share of India's GDP (over 50%), while agriculture still employs the largest share of the total (rural + urban) workforce in India.

• Employment data is collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

NOTE

• Important terms: Disguised unemployment (common in agriculture), seasonal unemployment, Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and the Unemployment Rate (UR) — all measured by the PLFS.

question: National Prophylaxis Program, which was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to address which of the following medical conditions /diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blindness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Prophylaxis Programme against Nutritional Blindness" was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to prevent blindness caused by Vitamin A deficiency among children. (नेत्रहीनता — विटामिन A की कमी से)

• Under the programme, massive doses of Vitamin A are administered to children aged 9 months to 5 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness, xerophthalmia, Bitot's spots and eventually total blindness. Sources: carrots, green leafy vegetables, milk, eggs and liver.

• The National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB) was launched in 1976, the world's first national programme of its kind, with the goal of reducing the prevalence of blindness.

NOTE

• Deficiency diseases: Vitamin A → night blindness; Vitamin B1 (thiamine) → beriberi; Vitamin B3 → pellagra; Vitamin C → scurvy; Vitamin D → rickets/osteomalacia; Iodine → goitre; Iron → anaemia. Hypercalcemia is an *excess* of calcium, not a deficiency disease.

question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 163.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 163 of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at its head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except where he is required to act in his discretion. (अनुच्छेद 163)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 153 — there shall be a Governor for each State.

• Article 154 — the executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.

• Article 155 — the Governor is appointed by the President.

• Article 156 — the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (normal term 5 years).

• Article 157 — qualifications for appointment as Governor (must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age).

• Article 164 — appointment of the Chief Minister and other Ministers by the Governor; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

• Article 167 — duties of the Chief Minister regarding furnishing of information to the Governor.

NOTE

• The corresponding provision at the Centre is Article 74 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President) — made binding on the President by the 42nd and 44th Amendments. Note that the Governor's discretionary powers are wider than the President's.

question: As per the reforms of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023, how many minerals have been removed from the list of atomic minerals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill/Act, 2023, six (6) minerals were removed from the list of atomic minerals in Part B of the First Schedule. (परमाणु खनिजों की सूची से 6 खनिज हटाए गए)

• The six minerals removed are: Beryl and other beryllium-bearing minerals; Lithium-bearing minerals; Niobium-bearing minerals; Titanium-bearing minerals and ores; Tantalum-bearing minerals; and Zirconium-bearing minerals and ores.

• Their removal allows private sector participation in the exploration and mining of these critical minerals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Amendment also introduced the concept of "exploration licence" for deep-seated and critical minerals, and empowered the Central Government to auction mining leases and composite licences for 24 critical and strategic minerals.

• These minerals are essential for electric vehicles, batteries, solar panels, semiconductors and defence and space technologies.

NOTE

• The parent legislation is the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, administered by the Ministry of Mines. The Geological Survey of India (GSI), established in 1851, is headquartered at Kolkata.

question: K Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 1999, for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1999 for his outstanding contribution to "Bharatnatyam". (के. कल्याणसुंदरम पिल्लई — भरतनाट्यम)

• He belonged to the famous Thanjavur (Tanjore) school of Bharatanatyam and headed the Sri Rajarajeshwari Bharata Natya Kala Mandir, Mumbai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra. It was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam and was revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra) and E. Krishna Iyer.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama, was established in 1952-53 and is the oldest national academy for the performing arts.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India/UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: A portion of landmass from the shore line up to the shelf break that is submerged under shallow water is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Continental Shelf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Continental Shelf" is the gently sloping, shallow, submerged extension of a continent, stretching from the shoreline up to the shelf break (where the slope suddenly steepens). (महाद्वीपीय मग्नतट)

• Its average depth is about 100–200 metres and the average gradient is less than 1°.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The continental shelf is the richest fishing ground in the world because sunlight penetrates the shallow water, supporting plankton growth. It is also a major source of petroleum and natural gas (e.g., Bombay High).

• Order of ocean relief features from the coast: Continental Shelf → Continental Slope → Continental Rise → Abyssal Plain (Deep Sea Plain) → Ocean Deeps/Trenches.

• Trenches are the deepest parts of the ocean — the Mariana Trench in the Pacific (Challenger Deep) is the deepest point on Earth.

NOTE

• Under UNCLOS, a coastal state's Territorial Sea extends 12 nautical miles and its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) up to 200 nautical miles. Continental Drift Theory was proposed by Alfred Wegener (1912) — it is a theory, not a relief feature.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in the three main dimensions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991, announced by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Urbanisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 (the New Economic Policy) rested on three main dimensions — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG). "Urbanisation" is NOT one of them. (एलपीजी — उदारीकरण, निजीकरण, वैश्वीकरण)

◦ Liberalisation — removal of licensing, quotas and unnecessary government controls on business.

◦ Privatisation — reducing the role of the public sector and inviting private ownership/disinvestment.

◦ Globalisation — integrating the Indian economy with the world economy through trade and investment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The reforms were announced on 24 July 1991 under Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, in response to the Balance of Payments crisis of 1991.

• Key measures: abolition of industrial licensing for most industries (retained for a few), reduction of the number of industries reserved for the public sector from 17 to 8 (later to 3, now 2), MRTP Act relaxation, and liberal FDI norms.

NOTE

• Earlier industrial policies: 1948 (first Industrial Policy Resolution), 1956 (the "Economic Constitution of India", classifying industries into Schedules A, B and C), 1977, 1980 and 1991. Urbanisation is a demographic process, not an economic-reform dimension.
